Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: a NEW scientific overview figure for the introduction of a research preprint, immediately before a table comparing three simulation setups.

Create ONE complete 16:9 landscape diagram, ideally 3840 x 2160 at the highest native resolution available. Clean, light opaque white background; navy sans-serif text; teal and amber accents; thin pale-blue panel boundaries. Match a crisp, flat scientific diagram style. All cells, grid squares, connection lines, arrows and text must be sharply outlined and easy to read when printed across a manuscript page. No glassy cells, transparency, blur, glow, gradients, soft shadows, glossy texture or tiny decorative details. Use three equal columns and a shared workflow across the bottom. Make the simulator internals visually prominent; avoid turning this into three paragraphs.

Title, large: "Three simulators: how we run the experiments"
Subtitle: "Different state variables, explicit updates, controlled replacement"

COLUMN 1
Heading: "TISSUE SHEETS"
Origin line: "Program-built spatial model"
Show three slightly offset but clearly separated small grid layers, labelled "Activity", "Reference" and "Writable bias". Use distinct flat teal, pale blue and amber squares to show spatially varying continuous states. The grids are schematic patches, not measured data.
Size line: "16 × 16 sites"
Show a magnified central site linked to its four nearest neighbours, with a small update-loop arrow. Nearby exact text: "Coupling + feedback + noise"
Below, show a simple spatial-record card crossing a dashed replacement boundary into a fresh, lightly outlined sheet. The previous sheet remains on the left of the boundary; no old cell is drawn crossing it.
Boundary text: "Reset body; pass record"
Bottom test line: "Capture • repair • writer placement"

COLUMN 2
Heading: "LOCAL FUNCTIONAL NETWORKS"
Origin line: "Program-built associative model"
Draw a small patch of a two-dimensional grid of circular activity nodes joined ONLY to their nearest neighbours. Links vary in flat thickness or teal/amber color to represent weights. One input port on the left is marked "Input"; two separate output ports on the right are marked "A" and "B". A pair of small cue boxes marked "+" and "−" points sequentially toward the ONE input, with exact text "Run both cues". This is a local weighted dynamical network, not a layered neural-network cartoon.
Size line: "16 × 16 sites; 512 weighted links"
Update text: "Weighted neighbours + noise"
In the lower half, two tiny activity snapshots, one marked "+" and one marked "−", feed into ONE small connection-weight record icon. Make the two-to-one writing route unmistakable. Label: "Write from both cue trials"
Then a short arrow carries that weight record across a dashed replacement boundary to a fresh node-grid with one or two nodes shown as missing/damaged. Only the weight record crosses; old activity does not.
Boundary text: "Reset activity; pass weights"
Bottom test line: "Teach • damage • rebuild"

COLUMN 3
Heading: "CELLULAR REGULATION"
Origin line: "BITSEY model + our assays"
Show three crisp, flat model cells linked by two-way junction arrows. In one cell show a simple internal regulatory loop and small ion symbols, with two clear labels "RNAs" and "Ions". This is a numerical cell-state model, not microscopy or a cartoon of cancer. Neighbours exchange influence through junctions.
Update text: "Regulatory + ionic equations"
Label under the connections: "Junction transport"
Below, show a small current-cell group contacting a separate fresh-recipient group. A later arrow leads to those recipient cells alone after donor removal; distinguish recipient outlines from donor outlines. Do not show a memory-card packet or cell division in this column.
Sequence text: "Contact → remove donors → test recipients"
Continuity line: "State continues in living model cells"
Bottom test line: "Rewrite • replace • pause transport"

SHARED BOTTOM WORKFLOW
Across the full width, a slim, clearly separated row with five modest icons and right-pointing arrows:
"Initialize" → "Step equations" → "Intervene" → "Continue" → "Measure"
Directly below: "Matched controls; fresh assays; repeat across declared cases."
Small readable footer: "Rules and schedules are supplied. Diagrams are schematic; no new results are shown."

Scientific constraints:
- The first two model families are numerical 16-by-16 periodic models constructed in the research program. The cellular family uses a published BITSEY source model with added assays.
- The record in spatial studies varies by experiment; do not imply all three field layers are always inherited together.
- The functional task is initially taught; renewal receives input cues, not target-output labels. Do not draw a teacher sending desired A/B values into the renewal writer.
- The cellular case carries history in continuing cell state and through communication into replacements, not in a separate digital packet. No division, DNA inheritance, treatment claims or success percentages.
- The bottom workflow describes controlled numerical experiments, not five biological stages.
- Do not include any figure number, numerical results, equations beyond the simple labels, invented screenshots or extra explanatory text.
- Keep every word inside generous margins. Use a small schematic patch for each large grid; no need to draw every one of the 256 sites.

Use case: infographic-diagram.
Create one polished scientific infographic for the active-forms section of a research preprint. Landscape 16:9, ideally 2048 × 1152 pixels, opaque white background with white corners. Match a modern scientific figure: large navy sans-serif typography, pale cyan panels, teal tissue cells and retained patterns, amber writing/feedback arrows, thin gray dividers and generous whitespace. Subtle translucent cell illustrations are welcome; avoid ornate decoration. Prioritize legibility and clear causal routes. This is a conceptual explanation of separate model experiments, not a measured plot or saved simulation output. Do not invent numbers or add text beyond the wording specified below.

TITLE, large:
Active forms

SUBTITLE:
Organization can help maintain the conditions for its own return.

MAIN LAYOUT: three equal, spacious panels across the page. These are separate experiments, NOT stages in one experiment; do not connect the panels with arrows. Each panel has a heading, a clear central diagram, and two or three short text lines. Keep the words large enough for a manuscript figure. Use cells and small spatial-record grids consistently, but make the experimental contrasts obvious.

LEFT PANEL
Heading: HISTORY CHANGES RESTORATION
Show a short left-to-right route inside this panel: supplied exposure to a simple teal spatial pattern, then an acquired reference field, then a partly disturbed tissue returning toward that pattern. Amber writing arrow from exposure/body activity into the reference; teal reading arrow from reference toward the later tissue. Do not imply that the particular exposure arose autonomously.
Labels: Experience / Reference / Later restoration
Main text:
Experience changes what the system later restores.
Control text:
Blocking writing or reading removes the exposure effect.

CENTRE PANEL
Heading: ORGANIZATION HELPS REPAIR
Show a paired comparison. Two small surviving tissue patches contain the SAME numbers of teal and pale cells; one has an organized teal band, the other has those same colored cells spatially scrambled. Labels: Arranged / Scrambled
Both patches interact with IDENTICAL damaged record grids, shown with the same missing/gray squares. Each branch writes an outgoing record; only that record proceeds across a small dashed replacement line into a fresh-body assay. Do not draw a surviving-body-to-fresh-body copying arrow. A tiny record icon on each crossing makes the information boundary unambiguous. The arranged branch can show a modestly clearer outgoing pattern, never perfect restoration or a numerical result.
Text above or beside the paired comparison:
Same damaged record. Same body values.
Main result text:
Surviving arrangement improves the record's later usefulness.
Boundary text:
Only the repaired record enters the fresh-body test.

RIGHT PANEL
Heading: WRITER RELATIONSHIPS MATTER
Show two matched small grids with the same starting record and writer-feedback geometry. In the left grid an amber feedback arrow addresses its corresponding teal site; in the right grid an amber arrow addresses a displaced site. This is a change in WHERE FEEDBACK ACTS, not merely a shifted picture of the final body. Labels: Aligned / Displaced
Text:
Same starting record; changed feedback placement.
Main result text:
The relationship changes reconstruction.
Small condition line:
Shared guide and machinery supplied.

LOWER CONTRAST STRIP, much shallower than the three main panels:
Heading: RECOGNITION DOES NOT GUARANTEE RENEWAL
At left, a small cellular-automaton grid leads to an eye/decoder icon with the text:
CA: an observer decoded history
At right, a separate small attempted writing loop has an interrupted arrow, with the text:
Tested live writers failed renewal screening
Use no percentages, bar charts, equal signs or shared numerical scale. These were different information-processing routes, not a matched contest. Small centered line within this strip:
Different transformations; not a resource-matched comparison.

BOTTOM TAKEAWAY, large navy:
Active contribution is demonstrated; autonomous maintenance remains open.

Small legible footer:
Separate model experiments. Conceptual diagrams, not measured fields.

CONSTRAINTS: Exact spelling, large readable type and ample margins. No numbered progression or connecting arrows between the three panels. No consciousness imagery, faces, mystical forces, metaphysical claims, DNA-as-record icon, invented data, flawless regeneration, or implication that the maintenance machinery evolved or maintains itself. Do not repeat the ruliad/Platonic-space strip from the companion discussion image. The focus is the causal evidence for active embodied organization. Keep the image visually clean and inviting rather than a dense methods poster.

History affects access

Organization helps maintain
the conditions for its return.

BOUNDED OBSERVER
Measures what counts as the same form
Thin gray DASHED observation arrows lead FROM the central body and FROM the fresh body TO this box. Do not draw arrows from the observer back to the bodies or record. The observer measures; it is not a lens through which patterns must pass to become real.
